# Exercise 1) Tidyverse: New Zealand

a)  Generate a table of vote count per year and type. Sort it by count.

```{r}
#
# Q1) A) Vote Count Table.
# 
data <- readRDS("nzge.rds")

table_data <- data %>% group_by(voting_type, election_year) %>%
  summarize(total_votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_votes))

kable(table_data,
      col.names = c("Voting Type",
                    "Election Year",
                    "Total Votes"))

```

b)  Focus only on the 2014 election. Report the proportion of votes for each party in the Candidate election.

```{r}
#
# Q1) B) 2014 election.
#
data_2014 <- data %>%
  filter(election_year == 2014,
         voting_type == "Candidate") %>%
  group_by(party) %>%
  summarise(votes = sum(votes,
                        na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(proportion = votes / sum(votes)) %>%
  select(party, proportion) %>%
  arrange(desc(proportion))

data_2014 %>%
  mutate(proportion = scales::percent(proportion)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Party", "Percent of Vote"))

```

c)  Produce a table for each year, indicating which party won the Candidate vote and which party won the Party vote.

```{r}
#
# Q1) C) Party and Candidate Vote.
#
party_vote_winners <- data %>%
  filter(voting_type == "Party") %>%
  group_by(election_year, party) %>%
  summarise(votes = sum(votes,
                        na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(votes,
            n = 1,
            by = election_year,
            with_ties = TRUE)

candidate_vote_party_winners <- data %>%
  filter(voting_type == "Candidate") %>%
  group_by(election_year, party) %>%
  summarize(votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice_max(votes, with_ties = TRUE)

winners <- full_join(candidate_vote_party_winners,
                     party_vote_winners,
                     by = "election_year") %>%
  arrange(election_year) %>%
  mutate("Candidate Vote Party Winner" = party.x,
         "Party Vote Winner" = party.y) %>%
  select(election_year,
         "Candidate Vote Party Winner",
         "Party Vote Winner")

kable(winners)


```

# Exercise 2) Tidyverse: Tennis

a)  How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
#
# Q2) A) 2019 Tournaments.
#
data_tennis_matches <- read_csv(
  "tennis-atp-sackmann-data/atp_matches_2019.csv")

print(paste("The 2019 number of tournaments was",
            length(unique(data_tennis_matches$tourney_id))))
```

b)  Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
#
# Q2) B) Repeat Winners.
#
data_tennis_matches <- read_csv(
  "tennis-atp-sackmann-data/atp_matches_2019.csv")

data_tennis_matches_final <- data_tennis_matches %>%
  filter(round == 'F')

print("We know that a player won more")
print("than one tournament as there are")
print("only 41 winners but 67 matches.")

print(
  length(
    unique(
      na.omit(
        data_tennis_matches_final$winner_name))))

print(
  length(
    na.omit(
      data_tennis_matches_final$winner_name)))

winners <- table(
  data_tennis_matches_final$winner_name)

repeats <- names(
  winners[winners > 1])

print(paste("The number of repeat winners is ",
            length(repeats)))
print(repeats)

max_winner <- names(winners)[which.max(winners)]
print(paste("The player with the most wins is ",
            max_winner))
max_winners <- max(winners)
print(paste("He has",
            max_winners))
```

c)  Is there any evidence that winners have more aces than losers?

```{r}
#
# Q2) C) Aces.
#
data_tennis_matches <- read_csv(
  "tennis-atp-sackmann-data/atp_matches_2019.csv")

data_tennis_matches_c <- data_tennis_matches %>%
  filter(!is.na(w_ace) & !is.na(l_ace))


data_tennis_summarized <- data_tennis_matches_c %>%
  summarise(
    mean_winner_aces = mean(w_ace),
    mean_loser_aces  = mean(l_ace),
    mean_difference  = mean(w_ace - l_ace)
  )

print(data_tennis_summarized)

print("Winners have more aces - 7.5 vs 5.79 average.")

```

d)  Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
#
# Q2) D) Win Rate.
#
data_tennis_matches <- read_csv(
  "tennis-atp-sackmann-data/atp_matches_2019.csv")

data_tennis_matches_winner_count <- data_tennis_matches %>%
  group_by(winner_name) %>%
  summarize(wins = n())

data_tennis_matches_loser_count <- data_tennis_matches %>%
  group_by(loser_name) %>%
  summarize(losses = n())

tennis_win_lose_count <- full_join(
  data_tennis_matches_winner_count, 
  data_tennis_matches_loser_count, 
  by = c("winner_name" = "loser_name")
)

tennis_win_lose_count <- tennis_win_lose_count %>%
  filter(wins + losses >= 5)

tennis_win_lose_count <- tennis_win_lose_count %>%
  mutate(ratio = wins / (wins + losses) ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ratio))

print(tennis_win_lose_count %>%
        head(5))
```

# Exercise 3) Visualization

a)  How many major and minor spikes in cases were there?

```{r}
#
# Q3) A) Major and Minor Spikes.
#
data <- read_csv("us-states.csv")

data %>% group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = sum(cases, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = total_cases)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Cases Starting in 2020.",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Number of Cases"
    ) +
  theme_minimal()

print("We see 4 minor spikes and 1 major spike.")
```

b)  For the states with the highest and lowest overall rates per population, what differences do you see in their trajectories over time?

```{r}
#
# Q3) B) Extremes.
#
data <- read_csv("us-states.csv")

state_rates <- aggregate(
  cases_avg_per_100k ~ state,
  data = data,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  FUN = sum
)

extremes <- state_rates$state[
  state_rates$cases_avg_per_100k %in%
    range(state_rates$cases_avg_per_100k)
]

trajectory <- data[data$state %in%
                     extremes, ]
trajectory <- trajectory[order(trajectory$date), ]

data$date <- as.Date(data$date)

data[data$state %in%
       extremes, ] |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date,
             y = cases_avg_per_100k,
             color = state)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = paste("Daily case rates: ",
                  paste(extremes, collapse = ", ")),
    x = "Date",
    y = "Cases per 100,000",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

Their trajectories are the same. They spike at the same time, but Main has a higher peak.

c)  Identify, to the best of your ability without a formal test, the first five states to experience Covid in a substantial way.

As covid came in a single starting wave and spread, we can deduce it from the graph. We look at the first 5 that had an average of greater than 1 per 100K.

```{r}
#
# Q3) C) First 5.
#
data <- read_csv("us-states.csv",
                 show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date))

first_substantial <- data %>%
  filter(cases_avg_per_100k >= 1) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  filter(!(state  %in%
             c("Guam", "District of Columbia"))) %>%
  slice_min(date,
            n = 1,
            with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

first_substantial %>%
  select(state,
         date,
         cases_avg_per_100k)

top_5_states <- first_substantial %>%
  pull(state)

data %>%
  filter(state %in%
           top_5_states,
         date >= as.Date("2020-01-01"),
         date <= as.Date("2020-3-31")) %>%
  group_by(state, date) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = sum(cases,
                              na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date,
             y = total_cases,
             color = state,
             group = state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Cases Starting in 2020",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Number of Cases",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Therefore, we conclude that Washington, Louisiana, Michigan, New Jersey, and New York were the first five states to experience covid in a significant way.
